plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE adjusted for sex/age
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human adipose bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control), Salmon-derived raw gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch, unpaired, with sex and age recorded per sample and the groups NOT age-matched. Because age and sex are known confounders that can differ systematically between treated and control (the profile explicitly flags age imbalance), the differential expression model must include both as fixed-effect covariates in the design formula rather than being ignored or regressed out in a separate step (regressing out and testing residuals would inflate false confidence, per standard practice). The plan: (1) QC on sample structure to check whether age/sex/condition co-vary with the first PCs and to catch any outlier sample before modelling; (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering; (3) DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age + condition, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the condition effect, BH-adjusted results with independent filtering at alpha 0.05; (4) an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as a robustness cross-check, reporting the overlap of the two gene lists as the higher-confidence set; (5) over-representation analysis (not preranked GSEA, per the grounded procedure for this situation) of the significant gene set against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome pathways staged in the environment, using the tested genes as the universe; (6) a consolidated report with fit diagnostics, the two-method overlap, enrichment results, and full reproducibility record. All steps are grounded in the returned procedure (snapshot sha256:ad61b0ba14...), with the enrichment step following the environment's own rule that this situation requires over-representation analysis on the significant list rather than preranked GSEA.
